newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mostly unchanged.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mostly unchanged in dull trading led by demand for giant brewer Bavaria.

Bogota's IBB price index edged down a slim 0.11 percent to 1,183.07 on volume above-average trading volume of 4.7 billion pesos. Medellin's IBOMED general price index slipped a razor-thin 0.01 percent ending at 18,016.92.

Bavaria, one of the eight largest brewers in the world, rose 0.38 percent to 7,830 on volume of 159 million pesos in Bogota, and closed up 0.89 percent at 7,870.10 on volume of 1.2 billion in Medellin.
Brokers said foreign funds and local investors alike had begun to buy back Bavaria stock after its recent dips on profit- taking.

Banco Ganadero, the country's largest commercial bank in terms of assets, failed to get any mileage out of remarks by its executive president at a news conference who said he sees it posting a solid net profit in the first half of 1997 despite the country's steep economic slowdown.
The bank's shares rose less than .01 percent to 6,803 on volume of 146 million pesos in Bogota, and remained at 6,800 in Medellin. ((--Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
